_comment: The search grammar, as data, so Dart and Python cannot drift apart.
Read by test_atlas_mcp.py (QueryGrammarTest) and by the Flutter app's
test/search_terms_test.dart. A change here must make both suites agree.
parse: query -> clauses, where clauses are ANDed and the terms inside one
clause are ORed. A term is [field, value]; value is already lowercased.
error_contains marks a query that must be rejected, and names a word the
message has to carry so the message stays useful without being frozen.
match: query + a synthetic asset -> whether it is a hit.

parse.why: a bare word searches everything
spaces are and
case folds
runs of whitespace collapse
empty is no constraint, not an error
whitespace only is no constraint
a field scopes the term to that field alone
the field name folds too
every field is reachable
a leading dot on an extension is noise
backslashes in a path term read as forward slashes
fields and bare words mix
and is a noise word, for people who type it
or joins the terms either side into one clause
or chains
or binds tighter than a space, so this is (a or b) and c
and after an or ends the or group
or works on bare words too
a quoted value keeps its spaces
a quoted bare term keeps its spaces
single quotes work the same
quoting makes a field name literal
quoting makes or literal
an = inside a value is kept, so only the first splits
a word containing = is a field, right or wrong: no silent fallback
a type value outside the vocabulary is refused, not emptied
and the refusal lists the types there are
an unknown field is named, not ignored
the error lists what is available
an empty field is an error, not a bare term
an empty value is an error, because it would match everything
an empty quoted value is an error for the same reason
a dangling or has nothing to join
a leading or has nothing to join
an unclosed quote is an error, not a silent truncation
look is reserved and says why it cannot answer yet
and names the pass it is waiting on
reserved before anything else in the query is judged

_animation_rule: Whether an unprobed FBX reads as an animation clip. The probe is the
authority wherever it has spoken; this is for the rest, and after a
rescan that is all of them -- model_kind was 0 of 34,801.
Measured against the probe on 100 sampled FBX: 98% precision, 100%
recall. The one miss was PolygonSyntyCharacter.fbx, the reference mesh
that ships inside the animation pack.
Only directories are read, because every false positive in the library
be a whole segment; `animation` may be a prefix.

animation_paths.why: the folder that holds 784 of them
the pack whose archive name says so, holding 721
a clip-named file inside the folder
a collision hull ships beside the clips and is still a mesh
animal is not animation -- this was a real false positive
nor this one, which is why only folders are read
a bare filename has no folders to go on

match.why: a bare word reaches the name
a bare word reaches the path
a bare word reaches the tags
a bare word that is nowhere misses
name= does not look in the path
name= does look in the name
name= is a substring, not a word
path= sees the filename too, because a path ends with it
but a folder is only in the path
path= does look in the path
tag= finds a tag
tag= does not reach the name
tag= is a substring of one tag
a tag the asset lacks misses even if the name has it
type= is exact
a type the asset is not
type= sees the resolved type, not the stored one
ext= is exact
ext= does not prefix match
rig= is exact
rig= on an asset with no rig misses
rig=none names the unrigged, rather than meaning unknown
two fields both have to hold
and one failing sinks it
or needs only one side
or across different fields
or with neither side misses
(a or b) and c, where c holds
(a or b) and c, where c fails
an empty query constrains nothing
a quoted phrase matches across a space in the name
a bare term cannot straddle name and path
nor path and tags
